the_one_code_path_this_wave_leans_on_tha.why_it_is_a_risk: Wave 28 was the last wave to build a multi-index excision and no wave has ever composed one with --ff.  Three lines carry it and none has been asserted: (1) the deletion loop must run in DESCENDING index order, or the second del addresses a list the first already shortened -- this wave's own pair (9, 13) would raise rather than lie, but --excise 9 --excise 11 in ascending order would delete block 9 and then whatever block 12 used to be, silently, at a correct-looking parameter count and depth; (2) and (3) every surviving module's layer_idx must be rewritten to its NEW position, because Lfm2Attention and the conv block both address the KV cache and the conv state by that integer, and two excisions renumber a longer tail than one does.
the_one_code_path_this_wave_leans_on_tha.and_wave_37s_dependency_is_load_bearing_: Lfm2Model picks each block's mask by POSITION in config.layer_types.  With blocks 9 AND 13 gone, blocks 10-12 shift down one slot and a full_attention block lands in a conv's index.  mx18_mask_probe.py measured the cost of not re-deriving that list: 0.0000 future attention mass with block 13 alone excised, 28.6% to 48.0% once anything shifts.

F1_the_X09_ladder_across_K.question: Wave 37 built ONE vocabulary rung on the block-9 body -- K=12,288 -- and it read TWO where its body read ONE, the first vocabulary fold in this campaign to gain a case over its own body, on a margin two tokens wide.  Does the X09-over-X13 advantage hold across K, and does anything hold signal BELOW 0.42x?
F1_the_X09_ladder_across_K.the_law_being_tested: DEEP_RECORD section 8.5, the flatness law: across eleven thousand rows the vocabulary fold does not change a body's count -- flat at 3 on ARCH.W896, flat at 7 on ARCH.CL1792, flat at 2 on ARCH.CL896, flat at 0 on ARCH.W896CL1792.  Its operative form for prediction is FLAT ACROSS K ON ONE BODY.  ARCH.V12CL896X09 reads 2, so the law says every other X09 rung reads 2.
F1_the_X09_ladder_across_K.what_would_break_it: any X09 rung reading anything other than two.  The CL896 body's own ladder already has one dip (K=16,384 reads 1 where every other rung reads 2) and one death (K=8,192 reads 0), so flatness on this axis has known exceptions and this is a test rather than a formality.

ARCH.V14CL896X09.reasoning: the flatness law, on the rung FURTHEST from the floor and therefore the safest of the three.  Its control on the unexcised body, ARCH.V14CL896, also reads 2.
ARCH.V14CL896X09.the_alternative_reading: ONE, the body's own count, if the K=12,288 +1 was a property of that rung rather than of the body.

ARCH.V10CL896X09.reasoning: the flatness law.  Its control on the unexcised body, ARCH.V10CL896, reads 2.  A read of two here is the FIRST case this campaign holds below 0.42x.

ARCH.V9CL896X09.reasoning: the flatness law, applied at the rung one step above the K=8,192 vocabulary death.  This is the prediction the wave is least confident in and it is registered at two anyway rather than hedged: the law says two, the body it is folded from holds one, and the rung below it on the UNEXCISED body is where the campaign's only vocabulary death sits.
ARCH.V9CL896X09.the_alternative_reading: ONE or ZERO.  A read of zero would be the second vocabulary death in the campaign and would bracket it on a second body.

F1_the_X09_ladder_across_K.what_this_answers_either_way: The X09-across-K answer.  If all three read two, the block-9 body carries two cases across a 5,120-row span of K down to 0.4071x and the wave-37 result was not a K=12,288 accident.  If they read one, the two-token +1 was specific to that rung and the sealed 2/15 frontier stands where wave 37 left it.

F2_the_excision_pair_at_depth.question: The pair law has never been tested on a deep body.  Blocks 9 and 13 are four apart; wave 17 measured that farther-apart pairs cost LESS (distance 2 gives 2/15, 2/15, 4/15; distance 4 gives 6/15, 6/15; distance 12 gives 7/15, monotone across two anchors) and wave 28 INVERTED it on a vocabulary base: ARCH.V19X13X09 (four apart) reads 5/15 and ARCH.V19X13X01 (twelve apart) reads 3/15, both at 0.689528x.
F2_the_excision_pair_at_depth.the_additive_account: On the CL896 body: ARCH.CL896 reads 4 (wave 15), ARCH.CL896X09 reads 1 (wave 37), ARCH.CL896X13 reads 1 (wave 35).  Each single excision costs THREE (DEEP_RECORD section 8.4).  Additive says 4 - 3 - 3 = -2, which clips to ZERO.
F2_the_excision_pair_at_depth.the_super_additive_account: Wave 28's V19 anchor: V19 reads 14 at 0.794570x, V19X13 reads 10, V19X09 reads 10 (each -4), and the pair reads 5 -- a joint cost of NINE where the solo costs sum to eight.  One case worse than additive.  Applied here: 4 - 7 = -3, which also clips to ZERO.

ARCH.CL896X09X13.reasoning: both accounts clip to zero and there is no third account.  A body that reads zero is not automatically a content death -- DEEP_RECORD section 4 -- and the artifact/content split will be reported whichever way the count lands.
ARCH.CL896X09X13.the_alternative_reading: ONE, if the two excisions kill overlapping rather than disjoint lanes.  ARCH.CL896X09's one lane is context-retrieval; ARCH.CL896X13's one lane is NOT context-retrieval, and two bodies that share zero of sixteen lanes byte for byte have no reason to fail on the same one.  That is an argument FOR zero, and it is why zero is what is registered.

ARCH.V12CL896X09X13.reasoning: the flatness law applied to a body registered at zero.  ARCH.W896CL1792 is the campaign's precedent for a fold that is flat at ZERO.
ARCH.V12CL896X09X13.the_alternative_reading: ONE, on the wave-37 exception -- the ONLY vocabulary fold in this campaign that gained a case over its own body did so on the block-9 body, and this child is a vocabulary fold on a block-9 body.  If it reads one it takes the sealed AND canonical 1/15 rungs from 0.420779x to 0.390512x, a 0.030266 move, which would be the largest single-wave frontier move since wave 35.
ARCH.V12CL896X09X13.note: this is the DEEPEST child this campaign has ever attempted, 42% smaller than the parent's half and 0.030 of stored ratio below the current floor.

F2_the_excision_pair_at_depth.what_this_answers_either_way: Whether the pair law survives a body that is already at 1/15 from either excision alone.  A zero says the deep zone has no headroom for a second excision; a one says the excision axis composes further than the count arithmetic predicts, on the one body where the vocabulary fold has already been seen to gain.

F3_the_lambda_1p0_rung_versus_body_separ.question: Wave 37 concluded that lambda 1.0's advantage is a property of the vocabulary rung AND the body, not of stored ratio.  It could not separate rung from body, because its only deep arm was at K=12,288 on the X09 body -- and K=12,288 is a rung where lambda 1.0 buys ZERO on the CL896 body too.  Wave 38's G3 is the one cell that separates them: lambda 1.0 at K=9,216 on the X09 body.

the_two_accounts.the_K_account: lambda 1.0's gain is a function of the vocabulary rung alone.  The one deep data point AGREES with it: +0 at K=12,288 on both bodies.  It predicts +2 at K=9,216 on the X09 body.
the_two_accounts.the_body_account: lambda 1.0's gain needs the unexcised CL896 body, and the X09 body's +0 at K=12,288 is the body refusing rather than the rung.  It predicts +0.

ARCH.V9CL896X09G10.reasoning: the K account, because it is the account the single existing deep data point is consistent with.  Registered as the control's count PLUS TWO: if ARCH.V9CL896X09 reads 2 as F1 registers, this arm reads 4.
ARCH.V9CL896X09G10.what_a_four_would_mean: a sealed 4/15 at 0.4070832855x, against the current sealed 4/15 record of ARCH.V9CL896G10 at 0.437349x -- a 0.030266 move on the deepest rung of the frontier that has ever moved.  It would also be the deepest THREE and the deepest TWO.
ARCH.V9CL896X09G10.conditional: BUILT ONLY IF ARCH.V9CL896X09 HOLDS AT LEAST ONE CASE.  A gain arm on a dead control measures nothing, and the order says so.
